name: Foxit
summary: PDF editing, OCR and organising priced under Acrobat, per user per year for the desktop editor or Editor+, which now bundles Foxit eSign. A perpetual licence is also sold, and the AI Assistant is a separate add-on.
best_for: individuals and businesses that want full PDF editing, OCR and organizing at a fraction of Acrobat's subscription: especially multi-seat deployments
skip_if: you only read and occasionally annotate PDFs (free readers cover it), or your org is contractually deep in the Adobe product line
honest_knock: Foxit's pitch is being the honest fraction of Acrobat's price, and on the headline numbers it delivers. The catch used to be that e-signing was always a second subscription. As of our 28 August 2026 reading that is only true below Editor+, which now includes Foxit eSign with 150 envelopes a year. The trap has moved rather than gone: buy the $129.99 Editor, then find you need signatures, and Editor plus standalone eSign Essentials is $249.99 a year against $159.99 for the Editor+ that bundles it. AI is still an add-on at $49.99 a year beyond the 300 monthly credits, and in September the FAQ said it is not sold for perpetual licences (the November FAQ no longer says so). Price the basket, not the first line.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user per year upfront, or $10.99 per user per month on an annual plan
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-11-27 on the Foxit PDF Editor pricing page and foxit.com/esign-pdf/pricing/: the Editor, Editor+, perpetual, AI Assistant, eSign and volume figures are unchanged; first re-verified 2026-09-22) PDF Editor is $129.99 per user per year, or $10.99 per user per month, with a 14-day free trial that asks for no card. PDF Editor+ is $159.99 per user per year or $13.99 per user per month, and bundles what used to be a second bill: mobile apps for iOS and Android, AI Smart Redact, cloud storage and Foxit eSign Essentials with 150 envelopes a year plus pooled eSign licensing. BILLING NOTE, first recorded 22 Sep 2026: the $10.99 and $13.99 figures are not month-to-month prices. They belong to 'Annual plan, billed monthly', a twelve-month plan. On 27 November 2026 the toggle has a third tab, 'Monthly plan', but its amounts load in the browser and are not in the page as we can read it, so we print no month-to-month price. Paying the annual plan by the month costs $131.88 a year on Editor ($1.89 more) and $167.88 on Editor+ ($7.89 more) without shortening the commitment. A perpetual licence, Foxit PDF Editor 14, is $209.99 once per user for Windows or macOS, covering editing, conversion, OCR, forms, security and fill-and-sign but not the web app, the AI Assistant, Smart Redact, the document management system or any cloud feature; Foxit's own FAQ argues the subscription is better value because it adds AI, cloud integrations, unlimited cloud storage, the full DMS and eSign integration, and notes that Adobe no longer sells perpetual Acrobat licences to new customers. Every Editor and Editor+ seat carries 300 free AI credits per user per month; the paid AI Assistant tier is $49.99 a year for 2,000 credits a month per user. On 22 September it was also offered at 'early access pricing' of $4.99 a month; that offer is not on the page read 27 November 2026. Credits reset monthly and do not roll over. The September FAQ said the add-on is not sold for perpetual licences; the November FAQ says instead that the paid tier 'works with any Foxit product, including the free Foxit PDF Reader', and does not mention the perpetual licence, so whether it attaches to Editor 14 is not confirmed. Standalone eSign still exists: Essentials $120.00 a year with 250 envelopes and 10 templates, Business $300.00 per licence a year with unlimited envelopes and templates; Foxit Agreements (read 22 September 2026, not re-read) is $359.88 per user a year paid in full ($29.99 a month) or $34.99 a month billed monthly. Volume discounts of up to 30% apply to orders of 30 or more licences across PDF Editor, PDF Editor+ and eSign, on subscription and perpetual alike, consolidating deployment into a single purchase order with one renewal date, standardised installation images and coverage for divisions and subsidiaries. An education discount is applied automatically at checkout when you register with a school email address; Foxit does not publish the rate. Reading note: the page's own translation table still carries superseded strings ('20GB cloud storage included', 'AI Assistant with 20 free credits/month') beside the rendered card text of unlimited cloud storage and 300 free credits a month. (2026)

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested the web editor of Foxit on the free account we created, with our own one-page test PDF. The file opened in about 3 seconds and a note could be added without a trial. Editing the text did not work: Edit Text showed an offer for a 14-day trial of PDF Editor+ at $159.99 a year, and its Free Trial button led to the desktop download page, so a trial could not be started in the browser. The pricing page now also has a Monthly plan. No trial and no checkout were opened. Account and start: we created the account and was already signed in on account.foxit.com; our AI assistant ran the test in our browser, in its own tab, on 19 November 2026 from 10:01 to about 10:20 CET, and took the screenshots at about 11:05. pdfonline.foxit.com first showed a create-account step; its sign-in button signed in from the shared session without any input, and the editor ran as Foxit PDF Editor Cloud. The interface opened in Dutch and was switched to English in the language preferences; the profile menu showed the free account status (Freemium in the Dutch interface). The cookie banner was declined and the tour skipped. The dossier name is Foxit and the review is on OSM (osm/foxit-review.html). An earlier look at the download route on the same day made no account and is replaced by this test. Core action, edit a PDF in the browser: our own one-page test PDF (Test Project quote, Prepared for Example Ltd., Total: 100 USD, no personal data) was uploaded at 10:05 and opened in about 3 seconds; a prompt about local fonts was answered with No. Editing text: Edit tab, Edit Text, then a click in the text opened an offer instead: Start your 14-day free trial of Foxit PDF Editor+ today!, Powerful all-in-one PDF and eSign solution, $159.99/year, Desktop, Web & Mobile, unlimited cloud storage and access to Foxit DMS, with Free Trial and Buy Now. So text editing did not work on this free account. Free Trial opened foxit.com/downloads for Foxit PDF Editor+, the desktop download route; nothing was downloaded and that tab was closed, and no card screen appeared. Comment: Comment tab, Note, a click on the page and the text Test note: check the total. worked without a trial, with Auto Save on. From upload to the blocked text edit took about 2 minutes, to a working note about 4 minutes. Export, only looked at: the Convert tab offers From Files, Blank, From Clipboard, From Web Page, PDF Portfolio, Combine Files, From Template, Export All Images, To MS Office (Word, Word 97-2003, Excel, XML Spreadsheet 2003, PowerPoint), To Image, To Other, To HTML, Recognize Text and Quick Recognition; several buttons carry an orange mark. Nothing was exported. Plans: On foxit.com/pdf-editor/pricing/ (foxit.com/pricing/ gives a 404), the FAQ says Foxit PDF Editor costs $129.99 per user per year and Foxit PDF Editor+ $159.99 per user per year, with monthly billing available from $10.99, and a perpetual licence, Foxit PDF Editor 14, at a one-time $209.99 per user; every plan starts with a 14-day free trial with no credit card required. The switch offers Annual plan, paid in full, Annual plan, billed monthly and Monthly plan. Editor+ adds the mobile apps, AI Smart Redact and Foxit eSign with 150 envelopes a year; the AI Assistant is $49.99 a year for 2,000 credits a month, and every account has 300 free AI credits a month; volume discounts reach up to 30% from 30 licences. Credits and limits: the account is on the free tier and no trial was started; My Subscriptions says No subscriptions. Click Buy Now to add one. The landing page names an upload limit of 10 MB, which was not tested. Checkout: not reached. Free Trial in the web editor leads to the desktop download, not to a card form, and Buy Now was not clicked, so no payment page, tax or total was seen. Cancelling: Account, Plans & Products, My Subscriptions, with My Orders, Payment Option Management, Billing Address Management, License Management and Device Management; there is no subscription, so nothing was cancelled. Profile has Delete Account at the bottom, which was not used. Not tested: eSign, OCR, an actual export, the workspace and AI Assistant, the card form and a trial start, which the web editor only offers through the desktop download. Clean up: the test PDF was kept only in the working folder of the session; the account and the note in the editor stay. The editor tabs could not be closed because of an unsaved-changes prompt and stayed open. Nothing was downloaded or paid. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: On the free account the web editor opens a PDF and takes comments, but Edit Text shows a trial offer. That offer's Free Trial button sends you to the desktop download, so a buyer who only wants the browser editor cannot start the trial there. Many buttons carry an orange mark for paid features.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session tested the web editor of Foxit on the free account we created, with our own one-page test PDF. The file opened in about 3 seconds and a note could be added without a trial. Editing the text did not work: Edit Text showed an offer for a 14-day trial of PDF Editor+ at $159.99 a year, and its Free Trial button led to the desktop download page, so a trial could not be started in the browser. The pricing page now also has a Monthly plan. No trial and no checkout were opened. Account and start: we created the account and was already signed in on account.foxit.com; our AI assistant ran the test in our browser, in its own tab, on 19 November 2026 from 10:01 to about 10:20 CET, and took the screenshots at about 11:05. pdfonline.foxit.com first showed a create-account step; its sign-in button signed in from the shared session without any input, and the editor ran as Foxit PDF Editor Cloud. The interface opened in Dutch and was switched to English in the language preferences; the profile menu showed the free account status (Freemium in the Dutch interface). The cookie banner was declined and the tour skipped. The dossier name is Foxit and the review is on OSM (osm/foxit-review.html). An earlier look at the download route on the same day made no account and is replaced by this test. Core action, edit a PDF in the browser: our own one-page test PDF (Test Project quote, Prepared for Example Ltd., Total: 100 USD, no personal data) was uploaded at 10:05 and opened in about 3 seconds; a prompt about local fonts was answered with No. Editing text: Edit tab, Edit Text, then a click in the text opened an offer instead: Start your 14-day free trial of Foxit PDF Editor+ today!, Powerful all-in-one PDF and eSign solution, $159.99/year, Desktop, Web & Mobile, unlimited cloud storage and access to Foxit DMS, with Free Trial and Buy Now. So text editing did not work on this free account. Free Trial opened foxit.com/downloads for Foxit PDF Editor+, the desktop download route; nothing was downloaded and that tab was closed, and no card screen appeared. Comment: Comment tab, Note, a click on the page and the text Test note: check the total. worked without a trial, with Auto Save on. From upload to the blocked text edit took about 2 minutes, to a working note about 4 minutes. Export, only looked at: the Convert tab offers From Files, Blank, From Clipboard, From Web Page, PDF Portfolio, Combine Files, From Template, Export All Images, To MS Office (Word, Word 97-2003, Excel, XML Spreadsheet 2003, PowerPoint), To Image, To Other, To HTML, Recognize Text and Quick Recognition; several buttons carry an orange mark. Nothing was exported. Plans: On foxit.com/pdf-editor/pricing/ (foxit.com/pricing/ gives a 404), the FAQ says Foxit PDF Editor costs $129.99 per user per year and Foxit PDF Editor+ $159.99 per user per year, with monthly billing available from $10.99, and a perpetual licence, Foxit PDF Editor 14, at a one-time $209.99 per user; every plan starts with a 14-day free trial with no credit card required. The switch offers Annual plan, paid in full, Annual plan, billed monthly and Monthly plan. Editor+ adds the mobile apps, AI Smart Redact and Foxit eSign with 150 envelopes a year; the AI Assistant is $49.99 a year for 2,000 credits a month, and every account has 300 free AI credits a month; volume discounts reach up to 30% from 30 licences. Credits and limits: the account is on the free tier and no trial was started; My Subscriptions says No subscriptions. Click Buy Now to add one. The landing page names an upload limit of 10 MB, which was not tested. Checkout: not reached. Free Trial in the web editor leads to the desktop download, not to a card form, and Buy Now was not clicked, so no payment page, tax or total was seen. Cancelling: Account, Plans & Products, My Subscriptions, with My Orders, Payment Option Management, Billing Address Management, License Management and Device Management; there is no subscription, so nothing was cancelled. Profile has Delete Account at the bottom, which was not used. Not tested: eSign, OCR, an actual export, the workspace and AI Assistant, the card form and a trial start, which the web editor only offers through the desktop download. Clean up: the test PDF was kept only in the working folder of the session; the account and the note in the editor stay. The editor tabs could not be closed because of an unsaved-changes prompt and stayed open. Nothing was downloaded or paid. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: On the free account the web editor opens a PDF and takes comments, but Edit Text shows a trial offer. That offer's Free Trial button sends you to the desktop download, so a buyer who only wants the browser editor cannot start the trial there. Many buttons carry an orange mark for paid features.
